description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
- Removed `Indx.Utilities.FileLoggerFactory`, and with it the package's dependency on `NLog` and
        `NLog.Extensions.Logging`. It was the server's NLog setup and had shipped in the package by
        accident: every consumer got NLog 6 in their dependency graph whatever logging they used, and
        `GetFactory` replaced `NLog.LogManager.Configuration` for the whole process, so a consumer on
        NLog who called it lost their own configuration. The engine's logging is unchanged: pass any
        `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILoggerFactory` to the `SearchEngine` constructor, from whichever
        logging system you use. If you called `FileLoggerFactory`, configure your logging system
        yourself and pass its factory instead.
      - Removed `Indx.Utilities.ConnectionStringHelper`, the server's lookup for where its two SQLite
        databases live. Like `FileLoggerFactory` it was server code shipped in the package. With both
        gone the package depends on `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions` only: no longer on
        `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` itself, nor `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Abstractions`. A
        project that used `LoggerFactory` and got it through this package now references
        `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` itself.
      - Changed: **an exception from a `ProcessMonitor.ProgressChanged` handler is recorded in
        `RecoverableErrors`** (source `ProgressChanged`, with the exception) instead of being written to
        `Console.Error`. The operation carries on as before, and the fault does not count towards
        `MaxRecoveryAttempts`.
      - Fixed: **the `ILoggerFactory` given to `SearchEngine` now reaches the indexing engines.** It was
        created and then dropped, so apart from two messages from `SearchEngine` itself nothing was
        ever logged. Expect from now on: an Error with the exception when an insert, update, delete,
        hibernate or index build fails (what the call returns or throws is unchanged; the background
        index build has no caller, so the log is where its exception shows), and Debug lines for each operation
        with the document key. Document text is never logged. The log prefix is passed as the
        `{Prefix}` argument rather than joined into the message, so a prefix containing `{` or `}` is
        written as it is, and a null prefix writes nothing.
      - Fixed: **a failure the engine catches is logged with its exception.** `Init`, `Load`,
        `LoadAsync`, `LoadFromDatabaseSync`, `Index`, `InsertJsonRecords`, `UpdateJsonRecords` and
        `DeleteJsonRecords` catch what goes wrong and report it through `ProcessMonitor` or the
        `error` string. The caller got the message, and the stack was gone unless they read
        `ProcessMonitor.Exception` (the error string carries none). Each now also logs an Error with
        the exception. What they return is unchanged.
      - Fixed: **a stream that breaks, or ends inside a record, fails the load.** Both used to report
        success with the records read before the break: the parser returned what the stream threw as
        a record with no document, and `Load`/`LoadAsync` took any missing document for the end of the
        stream. A dropped upload or a truncated file now fails, with `ProcessMonitor.Exception` holding
        what the stream threw, or an `ErrorMessage` naming the record the file ended in. `Init` given a
        stream that keeps throwing fails instead of retrying for ever.
      - Fixed: **`Load` and `LoadAsync` accept a stream that cannot seek** (a network or request body).
        They failed on the first record, because the parser read the stream's `Length` for progress;
        progress now stays at 0 for such a stream.
